concepts.name: Judging forging heat by color (red heat)
concepts.open_problem: Smiths read the incandescent glow color (dull red -> orange -> yellow -> white) to judge a workpiece's temperature and workability by eye, with no instrument; tacit because the right color depends on alloy, ambient light, and the specific operation, and is the gatekeeper for every forging/welding decision.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (searched forge/heat-treatment color apps; only static color charts and educational PDFs returned, no shipping app that reads steel color via camera for a smith)
concepts.verbatim_quote: In blacksmithing, red heat is the practice of using colours to determine the temperature of a piece of metal (usually iron or steel).

concepts.name: Watching temper colors 'run' (oxide-color tempering)
concepts.open_problem: After hardening, the smith draws temper by watching a thin oxide film change color (straw -> brown -> purple -> blue) and quenching the instant the target color reaches the edge; the entire window is only ~400-700F with a few degrees per color, so the judgment is fast, lighting-dependent, and very hard to quantify.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (only LightSpectrum Pro, an unrelated film color-temperature app, surfaced; no app detects steel temper-color run)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Heat colors develop in a narrow 400ºF to 700ºF temperature range with only a few degrees separating each color, making it difficult to stop heating at the desired color.

concepts.name: Forge-weld timing and temperature window
concepts.open_problem: A sound forge weld depends on hitting a narrow near-white welding heat and on flux/hammer timing: too cool and it will not bond, too hot and it sparks/burns and the weld is brittle. The smith judges the exact moment to flux, withdraw, and strike almost entirely by eye and feel.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (searched forge-welding apps; only guides, forums, and color charts, no tool that times/judges the weld)
concepts.verbatim_quote: care must be taken to avoid overheating the metal to the point that it gives off sparks from rapid oxidation (burning), or else the weld will be poor and brittle.

concepts.name: Quench judgment / interrupted (mar-)quench
concepts.open_problem: Choosing quenchant and reading the quench in real time (the hiss/spit, when to pull the part during an interrupted quench so it stops cooling around 400-500F) to harden without cracking; described as an art reflecting the smith's experience rather than a measured procedure.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (results were technique blogs and quenching sound-effect clips, no shipping product that guides/monitors a quench)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The interrupted quench is an improvised version of what industry calls mar-quenching.

concepts.name: Bloomery smelter decision-making (judging the bloom)
concepts.open_problem: In bloomery iron smelting the smelter continuously judges airflow, charge rate, ore-charcoal ratio, residence time, and slag condition by sensory cues to grow a good bloom and know when it is ready; this tacit decision-making directly determines the product but is not captured in any model for the traditional process.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (ML exists for MODERN industrial blast/ladle furnaces, but no consumer or hobbyist tool for traditional bloomery decision-making)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The decisions include airflow and charging rate, temperature, residence time in the reducing zone, ore-charcoal ratio, and control of slag characteristics, with results demonstrating the direct impact of these decisions during bloomery smelting.

concepts.name: Reading slag and tap-hole management
concepts.open_problem: Operators judge furnace condition from the slag's flow, color, viscosity, and the look of what comes out of the tap-hole, deciding when and how to tap; slag carries the signatures of furnace conditions yet 'reading' it for live control remains expert tacit knowledge.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen for a consumer/hobbyist tool; note a research robotic tap-hole machine (MIRS) exists for industrial furnaces, but nothing app-market and nothing for reading slag as a craft judgment
concepts.verbatim_quote: these slags encapsulate chemical and mineralogical signatures of the raw materials, furnace conditions, and technological practices employed by ancient metallurgists.

concepts.name: Ore roasting / calcination endpoint
concepts.open_problem: Knowing when an ore is adequately roasted/calcined, i.e. when enough sulfur/arsenic has been driven off without over- or under-roasting, is traditionally judged by fumes, color, and smell at the kiln; sources describe the purpose but not a quantified endpoint, leaving the completion call to operator experience.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The object of calcining or roasting certain ores before treatment is to dissipate sulfur or sulfides of arsenic, antimony, lead, etc., which are inimical to treatment.

concepts.name: Gold panning: reading the pan
concepts.open_problem: Distinguishing real gold from pyrite/mica and spotting fine 'colour' against black sand in the pan by hue, luster, and heft is a learned visual judgment; also reading iron-staining and soil/rock changes in the field to find gold-bearing ground.
concepts.app_market_check: shipping apps exist but for a DIFFERENT task: prospecting apps (Where to Find Gold, Digger's Map, Gold Maps, MineCache) are location/map databases, and 'Gold Detector App' camera mode is a gimmick beep, not real in-pan gold-vs-pyrite recognition; the actual reading-the-pan judgment appears unserved
concepts.verbatim_quote: Real gold is bright yellow (even when wet); pyrite is brassy/greenish, which helps distinguish it from fool's gold.

concepts.name: Fire-assay cupellation judgment
concepts.open_problem: Fire assay (fusion -> lead button -> cupellation -> weighing the prill) depends on the assayer balancing flux/temperature/atmosphere by experience so the precious-metal bead is recovered cleanly; accuracy is explicitly attributed to staff skill rather than to a fully automated decision procedure.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (a lab service, not a consumer app; no shipping product that performs/guides the cupellation judgment)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The key to an accurate assay is the skill and experience of the staff who are able to balance all the factors which may contribute to any variations.

notes: Both domains are genuinely physics-bearing and tacit-heavy; session-1 only touched 'forge welding heat by color' at a surface level, so these go deeper. LEAST AI-touched / strongest white space: forge-weld timing (none), quench judgment / interrupted quench (none), ore-roasting endpoint (none) -- no ML and no shipping apps found at all. Forging-heat-by-color and temper-color 'run' are very-low: rich static color charts exist but NO app reads the color live via camera for a smith (only an unrelated film color-temp app and gimmick metal-detector apps surfaced). Bloomery smelter decision-making is very-low for the TRADITIONAL craft, though ML is active on MODERN industrial blast/ladle-furnace slag prediction -- a clear penetration boundary worth flagging. Slag-reading and fire-assay are 'low' because adjacent industrial automation exists (e.g. a research robotic tap-hole machine; assay is a lab service) but the sensory craft judgment itself is unserved by any app. App-market check: gold-prospecting apps exist but only as map/location databases, NOT the in-pan recognition skill, so reading-the-pan is still open. WebFetch was 403-blocked on Wikipedia/Springer, so all verbatim quotes are taken from the exact text returned in WebSearch result snippets, not fabricated. Honest caveat: a few quotes (temper window, quench, gold) come from craft/industry sites rather than Wikipedia because Wikipedia snippets paraphrased; ratings reflect only AI/app work I actually saw, not exhaustive app-store crawls.
